title: Redesign the Operator's Board — re-roll 1 (bolder)
question: Fresh hand, foreign forms at full commitment, same committed world. Lock one — or steer and re-roll again.

options.label: The Patch-Bay Wall
options.lineage: telephone switchboard patch bay, played straight as the whole page
options.thesis: The page IS the patch bay: one jack per line on a full-width panel, published lines patched to the company bus with lit amber cords, drafts as empty jacks waiting for a cord.
options.viewport: Header, then the full jack panel — every line visible as a jack with its state — the bus rail and meter bridge carrying usage across the bottom, and the plug-in cord waiting in its cradle.
options.risk: Novelty eats operability if publishing, reading usage, or unplugging takes more than one obvious click.

regions.label: jack panel · one jack per line, cords to the bus
meter bridge · usage at a glance

options.label: The Control-Room Console
options.lineage: machine-room master control with its lamp mast
options.thesis: One lamp per line in a mast strip across the top — the whole fleet read in a single horizontal scan — and a scope panel for the selected line below.
options.viewport: Lamp mast strip under the header, then the selected line's scope panel with its usage, documents, and embed, switchgear actions in a fixed column.
options.risk: The mast reads beautifully at five lines and needs grouping before twenty.

regions.label: lamp mast · one lamp per line

options.label: The Tape Desk
options.thesis: The board as an append-only tape: every event a line stamped in time order — plugged, unplugged, conversation completed, credit alert — the newest at the top.
options.viewport: Header, then one continuous tape: event rows with mono timestamps and state stamps, the live lines' current state held in a fixed side margin.
options.risk: A temporal log buries the fleet's current state when the day is quiet and nothing moves.
